chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from Abū Ṭālib al-Anbārī, from Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah, who said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated to me, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Sayābah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
When the sun declines, the time of the two prayers enters.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose decline marks the prayer time
key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the two prayers, meaning ẓuhr and ʿaṣr
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined from the zenith; passed midday

ai.seo_question: When does the time for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayer begin according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when the sun passes its zenith, the time for both ẓuhr and ʿaṣr begins. It is a jurisprudential narration concerning the timing of salat (prayer), especially the shared entry of the time of the two daytime prayers.
